boundaries.why: a program that only configures webcpp::hash or names its errors names no C library (spec section 2.1)
Boost.Hash2's algorithms and HMAC need nothing but Boost (spec section 2.1)

the key derivations' layer and backends::hash2 include no C library's header: a linked backend's webcpp header comes in under its WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_<NAME>, so that a program that includes only a function's header gets its engine (spec sections 2.12 and 2.13)

argon2id and scrypt include no C library's header: backends::sodium's webcpp header comes in under WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_SODIUM, so that a program that includes only argon2.hpp or scrypt.hpp gets its engine (spec sections 2.10 to 2.12)

the digest and MAC families include no C library's header: a linked backend's webcpp header comes in under its WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_<NAME>, so that a program that includes only a family's header gets the engines of the backends it links (spec sections 2.12 and 2.15)
no XKCP header, and with it XKCP's generated config.h, reaches a program's translation unit: webcpp's adapter is the only way in (spec section 2.6)
backends::xkcp links XKCP alone, through webcpp's adapter (spec sections 2.6 and 2.12)
blake3 and backends::blake3 link BLAKE3's C implementation alone (spec sections 2.7 and 2.12)
backends::openssl links OpenSSL alone (spec sections 2.12 and 5.6)
the asynchronous family includes no C library's header: it calls the synchronous functions, whose headers bring a linked backend's under its WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_<NAME> (spec sections 2.13 and 11)

webcpp::asio is an optional heavy dependency: only the asynchronous family's header and backends::webcrypto's, which the convenience header leaves out, include it (spec section 11.2, CODING-GUIDELINES.md chapter 3)
